text:
jamie: Heads-up — after the rate policy rollforward at ~10:00PT we're seeing a spike of 429 reports and a few customers complaining about unexpected billing increases. I pulled ~6 tickets in the queue in the last 20m. Anyone on the rollout?
sara: Are you referring to the smoothing/refill window change from this morning? I saw some odd refill telemetry but haven't tied it to billing yet.
matt: yes, the smoothing change. We moved the refill aggregation to a 1s smoothing window (was 200ms) to reduce per-token jitter. We rolled from 5% -> 25% traffic at 09:45.
jamie: Repro from a customer: they run ~100 concurrent streaming requests and after ~60s they started getting 429s. They also saw billing events labeled `quota_adjust` that look like big jumps.
kevin: Can you collect request-ids and the X-RateLimit-* headers? Also need rate-service trace IDs.
sara: quick repro script I used: ```bash
for i in {1..200}; do curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -d '{"input":"x"}' & done
```
ops-natalie: Looking at service logs now — I see a path where the smoothing window code multiplies the effective refill tokens by 10 for clients that have `burst=true` in their profile. That would both allow a large short-term consumption and then cause immediate negative remaining which our limiter treats as exhausted -> 429.
matt: That explains the 429s. Why billing spikes though?
ops-natalie: Metering collects consumed tokens upstream. If refill is temporarily inflated, the meter records higher token consumption in that interval; downstream aggregation didn't account for the subsequent negative adjustments so the billing view showed a spike.
kevin: Ok. Action plan: 1) rollback smoothing change to previous config for all affected clusters, 2) flip `burst=false` default back while we patch the multiplier bug, 3) run a targeted correction job to adjust billing aggregates for windowed over-counts, 4) notify impacted customers and offer credits.
matt: I'll kick off rollback now. Rolling back to pre-rollout config on rate-service.
dev-bot: action: rollback rate-policy smoothing -> baseline (triggered by matt). Rollback started at 1719810600.
kevin: Once rollback completes, monitor 429 rate, X-RateLimit-Remaining behavior, and billing delta. I'll also open a ticket to run a sweep to find customers with >5% spike in token consumption in the 09:40-10:10PT window.
jamie: I'll draft a customer-facing note. Draft: "We're rolling back a rate-policy change that unintentionally increased short-term burst consumption for some customers. We're investigating related billing anomalies and will credit any verifiable overcharges. Please send request-ids, timestamps, and sample concurrency patterns to support@redwood.ai so we can prioritize." Thoughts?
megan: Add a request for "sample sequence lengths" and whether they used streaming or non-streaming endpoints. That helps repro.
jamie: Good call. Sending message to impacted customers now. Also creating internal postmortem ticket and tagging eng-runtime + billing.
megan: Can we add a short repro harness to the support playbook so CS can validate after rollback?
kevin: Yes — add the curl loop + a small Python asyncio example and the header checklist. I'll update the runbook.
jamie: Thanks everyone. I'll follow up with affected ticket IDs once the rollback is confirmed and with our proposed credit window. :thumbsup:
